questions.question: How many atoms are there in a methane molecule?
questions.questionHtml: How many atoms are there in a methane molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 5.

Key Points

  • The chemical formula of Methane is CH4.
  • This formula contains one atom of carbon and four atoms of Hydrogen.
  • Total atoms in Methane are 5.

Additional Information

  • The atomic mass of Carbon is 12.
  • The atomic mass of Hydrogen is 1.
  • The atomic mass of Methane is 12+4=16.

questions.question: Which of the following pair of mineral - need is correct? I. Iron - Formation of haemoglobin II. Sodium - Proper functioning of the thyroid
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following pair of mineral - need is correct?

I. Iron - Formation of haemoglobin

II. Sodium - Proper functioning of the thyroid
questions.solution: Iron is required for the formation of haemoglobin, a protein that carries oxygen to body tissues. Without adequate iron, the human body can't produce enough hemoglobin for red blood cells. On the other hand, sodium is important for the proper functioning of muscles and the nervous system, as well as for maintaining blood pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of 'elements - valency' is correct? I. Boron - 2 II. Fluorine -3
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following pairs of 'elements - valency' is correct?

I. Boron - 2

II. Fluorine -3
questions.solution: Boron has a valency of 3 because it tends to lose its three valence electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration. Fluorine has a valency of 1 because it needs to gain only one electron to achieve a stable electron configuration of 8 valence electrons. Valency is a measure of an element;s combining capacity and is determined by the number of valence electrons an element possesses.

questions.question: Lanthanides are a series of how many elements?
questions.questionHtml: Lanthanides are a series of how many elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 15.Key PointsLathanides:

  • The first element in the series, Lanthanum, led to the use of the word "lanthanides."
  • There will be 15 lanthanides if chemistry-based similarities are the main focus.
  • They were first discovered in Sweden's Ytterby in 1787.
  • They were found in a mineral called Gadolinite.
  • The basicity of lanthanides is one characteristic that influences how they interact with other elements.
    • The ease with which an atom can lose electrons is known as its basicity.
  • The basicity series for the Lanthanides is as follows:
  • La3+ > Ce3+ > Pr3+ > Nd3+ > Pm3+ > Sm3+ > Eu3+ > Gd3+ > Tb3+ > Dy3+ > Ho3+ > Er3+ > Tm3+ > Yb3+ > Lu3+

Additional InformationProperties of the Lanthanides:

  • They have melting and boiling points that are higher than those of other elements in the periodic table, although the trend is irregular.
  • The melting points approximately range from 800 °C to 1600 °C.
  • The boiling points approximately range from 1200 °C to 3500 °C.
  • Their most prevalent oxidation state is +3, yet they also exhibit other oxidation states like +2, +3, and +4.
  • Their density is high, ranging from 6.77 to 9.74 g/cm3.
  • It increases as the atomic number increases.

Important Points

  • There will be 13 lanthanides (Ce to Yb) when the gas-phase atoms are filled in, with a focus on the 4f-subshell.
  • There are 14 lanthanides if one concentrates on idealized electronic blocks.

questions.question: Which chemical compound, with the chemical formula CH 3 CH 2 Cl, is used as a blowing agent in foamed plastics?
questions.questionHtml: Which chemical compound, with the chemical formula CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>Cl, is used as a blowing agent in foamed plastics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chloroethane.

Key Points

  • Chloroethane with the chemical formula CH3CH2Cl is used as a blowing agent in foamed plastics.
  • It was used as a promoter chemical in the aluminum chloride catalyzed process to produce ethylbenzene. Now, it is not widely used in any of these roles.
  • Foam products are manufactured with chemical blowing agents that expand the plastic matrix before it solidifies.
  • Chloroethane is produced by hydrochlorination of ethylene: C2H4 + HCl → C2H5Cl.
  • Earlier chloroethane has been produced from ethanol and hydrochloric acid, from ethane and chlorine, or from ethanol and phosphorus trichloride, but these methods are no longer economical

Additional Information

  •  The chemical formula of 3-Chlorohexane is C6H13Cl.
  • n-Propyl chloride (also 1-propyl chloride or 1-chloropropane) is a colorless, flammable chemical compound. It has the chemical formula C3H7Cl.
  • Chloromethane, also called methyl chloride, Refrigerant-40, R-40 or HCC 40, is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH₃Cl.

questions.question: In the year 1817 ______ tried to arrange elements with similar properties into groups.
questions.questionHtml: In the year 1817 ______ tried to arrange elements with similar properties into groups.
questions.solution:
Dobereiner

  • In 1817, a German chemist Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner arranged the elements with similar properties in a group. 
  • Dobereiner Triad is based on three elements group. He was the first person who started grouping of elements on the basis of atomic weight.
  • The three elements of the triad were arranged in such a manner that the atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.
  • For example:- Atomic weight of Li=7, Na=23, K=39  the average atomic weight of 1st and 3rd element results in the atomic weight of 2nd element.
 
Element Atomic Weight Atomic Number
Li 7 3
Na 23 11
K 39 19

questions.question: Identify whether the given statements about p-block elements are correct or incorrect. Statement A: In p-block elements, the last electron enters the outermost p orbital. Statement B: The non-metals and metalloids exist only in the p-block of the periodic table.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify whether the given statements about p-block elements are correct or incorrect.

Statement A: In p-block elements, the last electron enters the outermost p orbital.

Statement B: The non-metals and metalloids exist only in the p-block of the periodic table.

options.text: Both Statements A and B are correct
options.html: Both Statements A and B are correct

options.text: Both Statements A and B are incorrect
options.html: Both Statements A and B are incorrect

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both Statements A and B are correct.

 Key Points

  • p-block:-
    • In p-block elements, the last electron enters the outermost p orbital.
    • The p-block elements have their outermost electrons in the p orbital, and the filling of these orbitals determines their position in the periodic table.
    • The p-block of the periodic table is a region that includes elements from groups 13 to 18.
    • This block consists of nonmetals, metalloids, and some metals.
    • The majority of elements in the p-block are nonmetals and metalloids, with metals being more prevalent in the earlier groups.

questions.question: Isobars are defined as:
questions.questionHtml: Isobars are defined as:

options.text: atoms of the same element having the same neutron number but different atomic numbers
options.html: atoms of the same element having the same neutron number but different atomic numbers

options.text: atoms of different elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers
options.html: atoms of different elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers

options.text: atoms of the same element having different atomic numbers and different proton numbers
options.html: atoms of the same element having different atomic numbers and different proton numbers

options.text: atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers
options.html: atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is atoms of different elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers.

Key Points

Isobars are atoms (nuclides) of different chemical elements that have the same number of nucleons. Correspondingly, isobars differ in atomic number (or number of protons) but have the same mass number.

Electrons:

  • Discovered by Sir J.J Thomson in the year 1897.
  • Previously named as cathode rays as they were supposed to be emitted from the cathode.
  • They are deflected towards the positive side.
  • They have high kinetic energy.
  • They are deflected by an electric and magnetic field.
  • It has a negative charge of

\(charge=1.602\times10^{-19} coulombs \)
\(mass={1\over 1837}\times 9.107\times 10^{-28}g\)

Protons:

  • Discovered by Goldstein.
  • Depicted first as positive rays because it seemed to emerge from the anode.
  • Mass of a proton is

\(1.670 \times 10^{- 24}g\)

\(Charge=1.602\times 10^{-19} coulombs\)​

Explanation:

  • Rutherford's discovery led to the discovery of nucleus.
  • He found out that most of the mass of the nucleus is situated in its centre and contains the positively charged particles protons.
  • The atom is otherwise empty and as electrons have negligible mass, the mass of an atom should be equal to the sum of mass of protons present in it.
  • However, it was seen that in Helium, there are only two protons, so its mass should be twice the mass of each proton = \(2\times 1.008 a.m.u\).
  • Experimental results revealed that it has a mass of 4.003a.m.u.
  • Hence, it was concluded that the nucleus has particles containing no charge but mass almost equal to that of a proton.
  • This was established by scientist James chadwick in 1932.

Additional Information

Rutherford's gold foil experiment:

  • He discovered the atomic nucleus and gave us an atomic model.
  • He directed alpha particles towards a metal sheet.
  • He saw that most of the alpha particles, which are positively charged particles, are not getting deflected.
  • Most of the alpha particles emerged undeflected.

  • Therefore, he concluded that most of the mass of the nucleus is situated in its centre and contains the positively charged particles protons.
  • Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain orbits.

questions.question: _________ is associated with spoilage, development of off-flavors, deterioration of textures, discoloration and loss of nutritional value.
questions.questionHtml: _________ is associated with spoilage, development of off-flavors, deterioration of textures, discoloration and loss of nutritional value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is food deterioration

Key Points

Food deterioration:-

  • It is a natural process that occurs over time in all foods.
  • It is caused by a variety of factors, including:
    • Microorganisms: Bacteria, yeasts, and molds can grow on food and cause it to spoil.
    • Enzymes: Enzymes are naturally occurring proteins that speed up chemical reactions. In food, enzymes can cause food to break down and spoil.
    • Oxygen: Oxygen can cause food to oxidize and become rancid.
    • Light: Light can cause food to discolor and lose nutrients.
    • Temperature: Temperature can affect the rate of food deterioration. Food spoils more quickly at warm temperatures.
  • Food deterioration can cause a variety of problems, including:
    • Spoilage: Spoiled food is unsafe to eat and can cause food poisoning.
    • Off-flavors: Food that is starting to deteriorate may develop off-flavors, such as sourness, bitterness, or staleness.
    • Deterioration of textures: Food that is deteriorating may become slimy, mushy, or tough.
    • Discoloration: Food that is deteriorating may change color, such as browning or fading.
    • Loss of nutritional value: Food that is deteriorating may lose some of its nutrients.

Additional Information 

  • Food processing:-
    • It can be any method used to turn raw food into food products.
    • It can involve one or a combination of the following: washing, chopping, pasteurizing, freezing, fermenting, packaging, and more.
  • Food preservation:-
    • It is the process of treating and handling food to prevent or slow down its spoilage. 
  • Food conservation:-
    • It is the practice of keeping food fresh and edible for as long as possible.

Zinc is a widely used metal that is commonly used in galvanizing steel, as well as in the production of brass and other alloys.

questions.question: Solubility of gases in liquids ______ with decrease in temperature.
questions.questionHtml: Solubility of gases in liquids ______ with decrease in temperature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer: increases.

Key Points

  • The solubility of a gas in a liquid depends upon the following factor,
    • The nature of the solute.
    • The nature of the solvent.
    • Pressure:- solubility of a gas in a liquid increase with the increase in pressure.
    • The solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas present above the surface of liquid or solution.
    • The temperature of the solution:- solubility of gases in liquids increases with decrease in temperature.
      • It is the reason that aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water rather than in warm water. Because the dissolved oxygen is more in cold water.

questions.question: What is conversion of oil to vanaspati termed as?
questions.questionHtml: What is conversion of oil to vanaspati termed as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is hydrogenation.Key PointsHydrogenation of Oil:

  • As vegetable oils have long chains and double bonds, they can go through addition processes. These substances are unsaturated. Vegetable ghee, also referred to as vanaspati ghee, is created by heating vegetable oils in the presence of Nickel catalyst, which changes the unsaturated fat into saturated fat.
  • This process is called the hydrogenation of oil.
  • While vegetable ghee is semi-solid or solid, vegetable oil is a viscous liquid. Since hydrogens are added in this instance across the double bond, the reaction is also referred to as an addition reaction.
  • As Nickel can absorb hydrogen, catalysts are utilized to facilitate rapid and simple absorption.
  • Simple absorption of atomic hydrogen and unsaturated fat on the metal catalyst is the mechanism behind this reaction. It should be pointed out that applying hydrogen gas under pressure is necessary.
  • The melting point of the oil or fat is increased after the hydrogenation process. Additionally, flavour degradation and oxidation resistance are preserved which increases the shelf life.

Hydrogenation:

  • The chemical process known as hydrogenation occurs when molecular hydrogen reacts with another substance or element, typically with the help of a catalyst like platinum, palladium, or nickel.
  • The method is frequently used to saturate or decrease organic molecules.

Additional Information

  • Pasteurization:
    • The process of pasteurization involves heating milk to a precise temperature for a predetermined amount of time in order to eradicate hazardous germs that may cause illnesses like brucellosis, typhoid fever, tuberculosis, and diphtheria.
    • Shelf life is extended by doing this.
  • Preservation:
    • The act of treating and managing food in a way that stops or significantly slows down decomposition and prevents foodborne illness while preserving nutritional value, texture, and flavor is known as food preservation.
    • Preservatives are usually added to accomplish this.
  • Homogenization:
    • The process of homogenizing, or dispersing a material uniformly throughout a fluid like milk, involves breaking down a substance—like the fat globules in milk—into incredibly minute particles. The cream will not float to the top of properly homogenized milk. The fat globules are broken up in the procedure by applying high pressure to force the milk through tiny apertures.
    • This process is done to make milk uniform and prevent separation.

questions.question: The dry cell is made up of an outer __________ container that acts as the anode.
questions.questionHtml: The dry cell is made up of an outer __________ container that acts as the anode.
questions.solution: A dry cell, commonly known as a Leclanche cell, is a type of primary battery used in devices like transistors and clocks. It consists of a zinc container that serves as the anode. The cathode is a carbon (graphite) rod surrounded by powdered manganese dioxide and carbon. The space between the electrodes is filled with a moist paste of ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) and zinc chloride (ZnCl2). In primary batteries, the chemical reaction occurs only once, and the battery cannot be reused after it becomes dead. This type of cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of Combination reaction?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a type of Combination reaction?

options.text: Adding of water to Quick lime
options.html: Adding of water to Quick lime

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Option 4, i.e Heating of Limestone.

  • A Combination reaction is one in which two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
    • Examples are the formation of calcium oxide by the combination of calcium and oxygen.
    • Calcium Hydroxide is formed by adding water to quicklime.
    • Combustion of coal and combustion of hydrogen are examples of combination reactions.
      • Coal burns in air to form carbon dioxide gas.
      • Hydrogen burns in the presence of oxygen to form water.
  • A Decomposition reaction is a type of chemical reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more new compounds.
    • When Limestone is heated strongly it decomposes to form calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which of the following equations is correct for one mole of gas?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following equations is correct for one mole of gas?

options.html: V1/V2 = \(\rm T_1^2/T_2^2\) (at constant pressure)
V1/V2 = \(\rm\sqrt{T_1}/\sqrt{T_2}\) (at constant pressure)
V1/V2 = T1 /T2 (at constant pressure)
p1/V1 = p1/V2 (at constant temperature)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is V1/V2 = T1/T2 (at constant pressure).

Key PointsCharles’s law:

It allows to set up the relationship between the changes in volume and temperature under constant pressure-

  • V1/V2 = T1/T2 [V1 and V2 are volume and T1 and T2 are different temperatures].

Additional InformationIdeal gas:

It is a hypothetical gas, consisting of molecules that are having negligible volume and their collision is perfectly elastically (means no loss of energy) and obeys gas law.

The Equation of State for an ideal gas is given by:

PV= nRT

Where, n = Number of moles of gas, P = Pressure, T = Temperature, V = Volume are the state variables and R = Gas constant.

Boyle’s law:

It allows to set up the relationship between the changes in pressure and volume under constant temperature-

  • P1V1 = P2V2 [P1 and P2 are pressure of gases and V1 and V2 are volume]

questions.solution: Phosphorus (P) has properties similar to nitrogen (N) as both belong to Group 15 of the periodic table, share similar electron configurations with five valence electrons, exhibit comparable bonding behavior, form compounds with similar formulas, and display non-metal characteristics.

questions.question: How many elements are there in the periodic table such that for every element name there is a single alphabet that symbolically represents it (for example, B-Boron, C-Carbon, etc)?
questions.questionHtml: How many elements are there in the periodic table such that for every element name there is a single alphabet that symbolically represents it (for example, B-Boron, C-Carbon, etc)?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is Option 3 i.e 14.

  • The periodic table is a tabular display of the chemical elements, which are arranged by atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties.
  • Elements are arranged from left to right and top to bottom in order of increasing atomic number. The order generally coincides with increasing atomic mass.
  • The rows are called periods. The number of electrons in a period increases as one moves down the periodic table; therefore, as the energy level of the atom increases, the number of energy sub-levels per energy level increases.
    Elements that occupy the same column on the periodic table (called a "group") have identical valance electron configurations and consequently behave in a similar fashion chemically. For instance, all the group 18 elements are inert gases.
  • There are 14 elements in the periodic table, represented by a single letter. They are
    • Hydrogen (H), Boron (B), Carbon (C), Nitrogen (N), Oxygen (O), Fluorine (F), Potassium (K), Yttrium (Y), Iodine (I), Tungsten (W), Uranium (U), Sulfur (S), Phosphorus (P), and Vanadium (V).

questions.question: Which of the following is a polar molecule?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a polar molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Water.

Key Points

  • Water has a polar molecule.
  • Unequal sharing of electrons makes water a polar molecule.
  • So even though the electrons from each atom are attracted by both oxygen and hydrogen, the electrons are a bit more attracted to the oxygen.
  • This means that electrons spend a bit more time at the oxygen end of the molecule.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Non-metal – Lead .

Key Points

  • Lead (Pb):
    • Lead has an atomic number of 82 and an atomic mass of approximately 207.2 u (atomic mass units).
    • It is a heavy metal that is dense, soft, and highly malleable, with a bluish-gray color.
    • Lead is commonly used in batteries, radiation shielding, and certain types of glass and pigments.
    • However, due to its toxicity, its use in household products like paints and pipes has significantly decreased to prevent lead poisoning.

Additional Information

  • Zinc (Zn):
    • Zinc has an atomic number of 30 and an atomic mass of about 65.38 u.
    • It is a bluish-white, lustrous metal that is brittle at room temperature but malleable when heated.
    • Zinc is widely used for galvanizing iron and steel to prevent rusting, as well as in alloys such as brass.
    • It is also an essential micronutrient in the human diet, crucial for immune function, wound healing, and DNA synthesis.
  • Platinum (Pt):
    • Platinum has an atomic number of 78 and an atomic mass of approximately 195.08 u.
    • It is a dense, malleable, and highly unreactive metal with a silvery-white appearance.
    • Platinum is extensively used in catalytic converters, laboratory equipment, electrical contacts, and jewelry.
    • Its resistance to corrosion makes it valuable in chemical and industrial applications, and it also plays a role in some medical treatments and devices.
  • Iron (Fe):
    • Iron has an atomic number of 26 and an atomic mass of about 55.85 u.
    • It is a silvery-gray metal that is prone to rusting when exposed to moisture and oxygen.
    • Iron is the most widely used metal, primarily in the form of steel, due to its strength and affordability.
    • It is also a crucial element in biology, forming part of hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body.
    • Iron deficiency can lead to anemia, a condition characterized by fatigue and weakness

questions.question: Hydrogen ions cannot exist alone, but they exist after combining with water molecules. Which of the following is the correct way to show hydrogen ions?
questions.questionHtml: Hydrogen ions cannot exist alone, but they exist after combining with water molecules. Which of the following is the correct way to show hydrogen ions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is H3O+Key Points

  • When hydrogen ions (H⁺) combine with water molecules, they form a hydronium ion (H₃O⁺).
  • This is because H⁺ ions are essentially protons (which are just hydrogen nuclei) and cannot exist freely in aqueous solutions.
  • They interact with water molecules to form hydronium ions.
  • The hydronium ion represents the protonated form of water and is the actual species responsible for the acidic properties in aqueous solutions.

Additional Information

  • HO⁻ (Hydroxide Ion)
    • ​The hydroxide ion (OH⁻) is formed when a water molecule (H₂O) loses a proton (H⁺).
    • The hydroxide ion is characteristic of basic (alkaline) solutions.
    • It acts as a base because it can accept a proton (H⁺).
    • Therefore, HO⁻ is associated with basicity or alkalinity rather than acidity.
    • For example, in a strong base like sodium hydroxide (NaOH), the OH⁻ ions are responsible for the basicity.
  • H₂ (Hydrogen Gas) 
    • H₂ is a molecule of hydrogen gas, which consists of two hydrogen atoms (H) bonded together by a covalent bond
    • Hydrogen gas (H₂) is neutral in nature and is not related to the concept of acidity or alkalinity.
    • It is a molecular species
  • H₂SO₄ (Sulfuric Acid)
    • ​H₂SO₄ is sulfuric acid, a strong acid that dissociates in water to release hydrogen ions (H⁺).
    • Sulfuric acid is one of the strongest acids.
    • When it dissolves in water, it releases a significant amount of hydrogen ions (H⁺), which lowers the pH and makes the solution acidic.
    • However, sulfuric acid itself is not a direct representation of hydrogen ions in their purest form; it is a compound that produces H⁺ ions in solution.

questions.question: Which of the following metal salts is responsible for permanent hardness in water?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following metal salts is responsible for permanent hardness in water?

options.html: Ca(HCO3)2
CaCl2

questions.solution:
The correct answer is CaCl2

Key Points

  • CaCl2 (calcium chloride) is responsible for permanent hardness in water.
  • Hard water has a high mineral content.
    • It is formed when water percolates through the deposits of chalk and limestone, which are made up of magnesium and calcium carbonates.
    • It does not lather with soap, so it is not suitable for laundry purposes.
    • It can damage boilers because it causes salt to build and lowers the boiler's performance.
    • Although hard water is safe to drink, consuming it frequently can cause a number of issues, including:
      • skin strain
      • Water appliances have to work harder, which raises the cost of water.
      • Spots show up on linens and clothing.

Additional Information

  • There are two categories of water hardness:
    • 1. Temporary Hardness of Water:
      • Water becomes momentarily hard due to the carbonates of calcium and magnesium present.
      • In this instance, boiling the water will eliminate the hardness.
      • The soluble salts of Mg(HCO3)2 are changed into the insoluble Mg(OH)2 when water is boiled; this precipitates and is eliminated.
      • We obtain soft water as a result of filtration.
    • 2. Permanent Hardness of Water:
      • The presence of soluble compounds of calcium and magnesium in water in the form of chlorides and sulfides is referred to as permanent hardness because boiling cannot eliminate this hardness.
      • By using washing soda to treat the water, we may get rid of this hardness.
      • When washing soda combines with the calcium and magnesium sulfide and chloride salts, insoluble carbonates are created, turning hard water into soft water.

questions.question: 'At constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is proportional to the partial pressure of the gas collected above the surface of the liquid or solution'. What is this rule?
questions.questionHtml: 'At constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is proportional to the partial pressure of the gas collected above the surface of the liquid or solution'. What is this rule?
questions.solution:
Option 1 is correct, i.e. Henry's law.

  • Henry’s law, states that the weight of a gas dissolved by a liquid is proportional to the pressure of the gas upon the liquid.
  • The law, which was first formulated in 1803 by the English physician and chemist William Henry, holds only for dilute solutions and low gas pressures.

Extra facts:

  • Charles' law: A law stating that the volume of an ideal gas at constant pressure is directly proportional to the absolute temperature.
  • Boyle's law: A law stating that the pressure of a given mass of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its volume at a constant temperature.
  • Newton's law:
    • Newton’s first law: states that, if a body is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless it is acted upon by a force.
    • Newton’s second law: States that the time rate of change of the momentum of a body is equal in both magnitude and direction to the force imposed on it.
    • Newton’s third law: states that when two bodies interact, they apply forces to one another that are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.question: The chemical reaction which involves addition of _______ or removal of ________ is called reduction.
questions.questionHtml: The chemical reaction which involves addition of _______ or removal of ________ is called reduction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is hydrogen, oxygen.

Key Points

  • Reduction Reaction:
    • The chemical reaction which involves addition of hydrogen or removal of oxygen is called reduction.
    • The process of reduction is a type of chemical reaction in which the electron density of an atom or molecule is increased.
    • Reduction reactions are opposite to oxidation reactions, which involve the loss of electrons or increase in the oxidation state of an atom or molecule.
    • Reduction reactions are widely used in industrial processes such as the production of metals and organic chemicals.
  • Redox reaction:
    • Redox reactions are chemical processes involving oxidation and reduction in which the oxidation states of the reactants change. 
    • In a chemical reaction, the material that is being reduced is referred to as the oxidizing agent, and the substance that is being oxidized is referred to as the reducing agent. 

Additional Information

  • Photosynthesis:
    • It is the biological process by which plants convert sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose (a form of sugar) and oxygen. 
    • This chemical reaction which involves addition of Carbon Dioxide and removal of Oxygen.
    • This process takes place in specialized structures within plant cells called chloroplasts, which contain a pigment called chlorophyll that gives plants their green color.
    • During photosynthesis, chlorophyll absorbs the energy from sunlight.
    • This energy is used to power a series of chemical reactions that convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose.
  • Other Type of Chemical reactions are:
    • Bi-displacement reaction is also known as the double displacement reaction.
      • It involves two reactants exchanging their ions to form two new products.
      • For example, potassium nitrate reacts with aluminium chloride and forms aluminium nitrate and potassium chloride. 
      • Reaction: KNO3 + AlCl3 ↔️    Al(NO3)3 + KCl
    • Displacement reaction is also known as the single replacement reaction.
      • It involves a more reactive element displacing a less reactive element from its compound.
      • The reaction of potassium with magnesium chloride is an example of a single displacement reaction.
      • Reaction: 2K + MgCl2 → 2KCl + Mg
    • Combination reaction is also known as the synthesis reaction.
      • It involves two or more reactants combining to form a single product.
      • For example, when we burn magnesium ribbon (or magnesium), it gives a gray-black ash of magnesium oxide.
      • Reaction: Mg + O2 → MgO

questions.question: Select the correct order of processes used for water purification in waterworks. 1. Filtration 2. Chlorination 3. Suspended impurity sedimentation 4. Solid impurity sedimentation
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct order of processes used for water purification in waterworks.
1. Filtration
2. Chlorination
3. Suspended impurity sedimentation
4. Solid impurity sedimentation
questions.solution: The correct order for water purification in waterworks is solid impurity sedimentation, suspended impurity sedimentation, filtration, and chlorination. Solid impurity sedimentation removes large particles, while suspended impurity sedimentation uses coagulants like alum to settle smaller particles. Filtration eliminates fine impurities, and chlorination disinfects water by killing harmful microorganisms and pathogens.
